dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: That's not clever enough... Now, how did he carry out the crime...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Carry out the crime?

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: Ah, please don't misunderstand me, my friend. I'm thinking through the culprit's method for my next novel.

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: To me, motive and interpersonal drama are important, of course, but they'll never outweigh the credibility of the method itself.

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: For example, say the core trick is this: there are only seven victims, yet the killer creates the illusion that eight people have died, misleading everyone into believing the culprit is among the dead...

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: Now imagine telling the reader at the very end, "Oh, actually, the killer is an incredibly powerful mage who brought a statue to life to fake the eighth corpse!"

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: Or maybe, "The killer can observe other worlds and casually pulled a body over from another reality"...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...The readers will come and beat you up, won't they?

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: Right! Which is why the method needs to be thought through again and again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: Mm, goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: A few days ago, I actually came up with the perfect crime while I was drinking under the windmill, looking for inspiration.

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, I was too drunk. I only managed to scrawl out a few words on a scrap of paper... By the time I sobered up, it was gone.

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: All I remember now is the chirping of birds above my head... Was it a dream? Or was it real...

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: The method, the method... Ugh, why can't I remember it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll leave you to it...

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: Come on, brain... work with me!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about Lohen...

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: My last discussion with Mr. Lohen was truly enlightening! I never thought there could be a knight who's an expert in crime.

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: I wonder what he was doing before becoming a knight... Maybe he was a writer too?

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: I've got a perfect crime to discuss with him next time we meet — Two accomplices, communicating with each other through letters...

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: While the true culprit... is the third person hiding in the backdrop of said correspondence!

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: ...Sir Knight! I swear, it's just a plot point for a novel! It wasn't a "master plan" for a crime or anything.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I understand, Mr. Uchida, I hear you loud and clear. No need to get so worked up. Why don't you have some tea and calm down first?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: According to intel from a key informant... your manuscript really doesn't look like a "master plan" for a crime. After all, it would be extremely impractical to pull off.

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: Excuse me!? What do you mean "impractical"!? If you're so brilliant, tell me what's wrong!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Too many conditions, and the steps are far too convoluted. You'd need a poison that fits your exact needs, not to mention a building that matches your specific requirements...

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: Uhhh...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: One tiny slip at any stage and the whole thing will be exposed instantly, won't it? Not to mention, the setup is so convoluted that it's a chore just understanding it all.

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: ...Now that you mention it, you do have a point. In that case, how should I improve this?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I suppose I do dabble in medicine from time to time. How about we try a bit of this... and then... a little of that?

dialogues.speaker: Uchida Kotaro
dialogues.text: Oh! Honestly, Sir Knight, this job is beneath you! You're far too brilliant!
